You may RUN it to observe behavior (e.g. `/tmp/orig -e 'console.log(...)'` or `/tmp/orig /tmp/x/file.js`), but you MUST NOT disassemble/decompile it, read its bytes, use strace/ltrace or any tracing on it, search the internet, or download anything (there is no network anyway). The main crate lives at /workspace (Cargo.toml, src/main.rs) and is being written concurrently by someone else. DO NOT edit any file in /workspace except the ones assigned to you below; never run /workspace/compile.sh; never write to /workspace/executable. Develop and test in your own scratch crate (e.g. /tmp/regexp_dev/, created with `cargo new`), then copy the final source files into the assigned location. Your modules must compile as modules of a Rust 2021 crate using only `std` (no external crates; avoid `unsafe`), ideally warning-free. Keep every scratch script (Python/shell/JS/Perl) under /tmp, never in /workspace (generated Rust table files are fine inside your module dirs). Modest #[cfg(test)] unit tests are welcome.

YOUR TASK has two parts.

PART 1 — Unicode utilities at /workspace/src/unicode/ (mod.rs + generated table files), mounted from main.rs as `mod unicode;`:
```rust
pub fn is_id_start(c: u32) -> bool;     // ID_Start (+ '$' and '_' are handled by the caller, but you may also expose is_js_id_start/is_js_id_continue that include $, _, ZWNJ/ZWJ for continue)
pub fn is_id_continue(c: u32) -> bool;  // ID_Continue
pub fn is_js_whitespace(c: u32) -> bool; // WhiteSpace per ECMA-262 (TAB VT FF SP NBSP ZWNBSP + Zs)
pub fn is_line_terminator(c: u32) -> bool;
pub fn general_category(c: u32) -> GeneralCategory (enum) ; // as needed by \p{} 
pub fn normalize(s: &[u16], form: NormForm /* Nfc, Nfd, Nfkc, Nfkd */) -> Vec<u16>; // String.prototype.normalize (lone surrogates pass through)
pub fn to_upper_full(c: u32) -> impl Iterator / small array; to_lower_full(c) ; simple_case_fold(c) -> u32; // you may use std's char::to_uppercase/to_lowercase where they are correct

```
Generate tables with python3's unicodedata (note its Unicode version) and perl for Script/Script_Extensions/binary properties if needed; store them compactly as sorted range arrays (`&[(u32,u32)]`) with binary search. Keep total generated source size reasonable (a few hundred KB max).

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Debug)]
pub struct RegexFlags { pub has_indices: bool, pub global: bool, pub ignore_case: bool, pub multiline: bool, pub dot_all: bool, pub unicode: bool, pub unicode_sets: bool, pub sticky: bool }
pub fn parse_flags(flags: &[u16]) -> Result<RegexFlags, String>;  // Err = exact message the original's SyntaxError uses for invalid/duplicate flags (and u+v together)
pub struct CompiledRegex { ... }   // must be cheap to share (wrap internals in Rc if needed)
pub fn compile(pattern: &[u16], flags: RegexFlags) -> Result<CompiledRegex, String>; // Err = exact SyntaxError message the original uses for that pattern
impl CompiledRegex {
  pub fn capture_count(&self) -> usize;                 // capturing groups, not counting group 0
  pub fn group_names(&self) -> Vec<(Vec<u16>, Vec<usize>)>; // named groups in source order: name -> group indices (ES2025 allows the same name in different alternatives)
  pub fn exec(&self, input: &[u16], last_index: usize) -> Option<Vec<Option<(usize, usize)>>>;
    // RegExpBuiltinExec core: search for a match starting at last_index (if sticky: only AT last_index); returns spans (in UTF-16 code-unit indices) for groups 0..=capture_count. In unicode/v mode, matching works on code points (surrogate pairs), but indices are code units.
}
pub fn escape_source(pattern: &[u16]) -> Vec<u16>; // value of RegExp.prototype.source as the original renders it (e.g. "" -> "(?:)", "/" -> "\/", line terminators escaped) — verify vs the original
```
Semantics: full ECMAScript 2025 regular expressions — alternation, greedy/lazy quantifiers incl. {n,m}, character classes with ranges and escapes (\d\w\s\D\W\S, \b\B, \cX, \0, \xHH, \uHHHH, \u{...} in u-mode, identity escapes), dot / dotAll, ^ $ with multiline, capturing / non-capturing / named groups `(?<name>...)`, backreferences \1..\99 and \k<name> (including forward refs and refs to unmatched groups which match empty), lookahead and lookbehind (positive/negative; lookbehind matches backwards per spec), Annex B web-compat syntax in non-unicode mode (legacy octal escapes, invalid `{` treated as literal, `]` literal, \c edge cases, quantifiable lookahead, etc.), unicode property escapes \p{...}/\P{...} (General_Category values & aliases, Script=/sc=, Script_Extensions=/scx=, and binary properties like Alphabetic, White_Space, ASCII, Any, Assigned, Uppercase, Lowercase, ID_Start, ID_Continue, Emoji, Emoji_Presentation, Extended_Pictographic... whatever you can get tables for), the `v` flag (class set operations `--` `&&`, nested classes, \q{...} string literals, properties of strings if feasible), case-insensitive matching with correct Canonicalize semantics (non-unicode: toUppercase-based mapping per spec with the "don't map non-ASCII to ASCII" rule; unicode: simple case folding), and the ES2025 pattern modifiers `(?i:...)`, `(?-i:...)`, `(?ims-ims:...)`. Compile to an internal program executed by a backtracking VM with an explicit stack. Add cheap optimizations (literal prefix scan / first-char set, anchored start) so typical patterns run fast; aim for at least ~10M simple steps/sec.

Exact error messages: probe the original for many invalid patterns, e.g. `try { new RegExp("[") } catch (e) { console.log(e.name + ": " + e.message) }` (it printed "SyntaxError: unterminated character class"), and for: unterminated group, nothing to repeat (`*a`, `a**`), invalid group `(?`, invalid escape in u-mode `\c`, `\u{110000}`, numbers out of order in quantifier `a{2,1}`, range out of order `[z-a]`, invalid named reference `\k<x>`, duplicate group name, invalid property name `\p{Foo}`, lone `)` , invalid flags `new RegExp("a","gg")`, `new RegExp("a","x")`, u+v together, lookbehind quantifier in u-mode, etc. Also check whether the original reports errors for regex LITERALS in source at parse time with the same message (e.g. `/a**/` in a script) — just report what you see. Record these messages in your code.

Validation: build a decent differential test corpus (hundreds of pattern/flags/input triples covering all features) and compare your engine's results with the original by running JS like `JSON.stringify(/pat/flags.exec(str))` and `str.match/matchAll/replace/split` in the original (and node v18 as a secondary reference for standard semantics; node 18 lacks some ES2024/2025 features like `v` and modifiers — the original is the truth there). In your final reply, summarize the API, test coverage, and known gaps.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. # lumen

A from-scratch JavaScript **engine** in Rust — std only, zero dependencies — and a
**runtime** being built on top of it, the way Node/Deno/Bun wrap a JS engine with an event
loop and host APIs. Every crate in the workspace is std-only: no `tokio`, `mio`, `libc`,
`rustyline`, `serde`, or any other third-party dependency, anywhere.

## The engine (`crates/lumen`)

A lexer, parser, and **three execution tiers**:

- a **tree-walking interpreter** — the reference oracle: the spec semantics live here, and
  every other tier must match it observably (a differential fuzzer, `lumen-difftest`, holds
  them to that);
- an opt-in **bytecode VM** — functions compile whole (or not at all — no deoptimization) to
  a stack machine with slot-homed locals, per-site inline caches for property and free-name
  access backed by object shapes (hidden classes), and dense-array element fast paths;
- a **native template JIT** — bytecode lowers to real ARM64 machine code on macOS, Linux,
  and Windows, with a correctness-first x86-64 backend on Intel macOS, Linux, and Windows:
  per-op templates with the interpreter as the shared slow path, inline-cache reads baked
  into the instruction stream, fused compare-and-branch, exact-`ToInt32` bitops, and numeric
  *register chains* that keep runs of arithmetic entirely in FP registers. The full set of
  inline fast paths currently lives in the ARM64 backend; x86-64 starts with native control
  flow and checked per-op helpers. Other architectures degrade to the bytecode VM.

Tier selection: `--tier=interp|bytecode|jit` (**jit is the default**; where the JIT is
unavailable it degrades to the bytecode VM). Functions tier up after a call-count threshold —
immediately if the body contains a loop. Force the reference tree-walker with `--tier=interp`
(or `LUMEN_TIER=interp`).

The language surface: generators and `async`/`await` running on stackful coroutines (async
bodies suspend on the bytecode VM itself), full `RegExp` (including `\p{…}` and inline
modifiers), typed arrays, `Proxy`/`Reflect`, ES modules (top-level await, `import defer`,
source phase), `Intl`, and `Temporal`.

`Intl` (ECMA-402) and `Temporal` are behind the default-on `intl` and `temporal` Cargo features.
The CLDR data tables included by `intl` are the largest single contributor to binary size (~3 MB
of the release binary). Build with `--no-default-features` for a small engine: the `Intl` and
`Temporal` globals are absent, `Date.prototype.toTemporalInstant` is omitted, and the `toLocale*`
methods degrade to their locale-independent forms, the way engines built without i18n do. Either
feature can be enabled independently.

On dependencies and `unsafe`: the workspace stays std-only — the JIT maps executable memory
through raw platform declarations (`mmap`/`mprotect`, macOS `MAP_JIT`, or Windows
`VirtualAlloc`/`VirtualProtect`) rather than libc. Pages are writable only while code is copied,
then executable/read-only, and instruction caches are synchronized where required. The
interpreter and bytecode VM are safe Rust; `unsafe` is concentrated where machine
code meets the object graph (the JIT's executable pages and its templates' raw reads — every
baked offset is *measured at runtime* against the live types and fails closed to the checked
helper if anything doesn't hold) and in the N-API addon loader's `dlopen` bridge.

**Passes 100% of [tc39/test262](https://github.com/tc39/test262): 53,400/53,400** (including
annexB, intl402, and staging) — on the default JIT tier and under `LUMEN_TIER=interp`.

Extracted from — and used by — the [lucid-softworks/browser](https://github.com/lucid-softworks/browser)
engine as its JS backend (`backend-lumen`), with full git history.

## The runtime

A curated `embed` API on the engine exposes just enough — native-function registration, a
typed host-state slot, and event-loop hooks — for a runtime layer to be assembled from
independent op crates, without leaking the interpreter's internals into the published API.
On top of that:

- **Event loop** (`lumen-runtime`) — a single loop thread owns the (`!Send`) engine; blocking
  work runs on a std thread pool and completes back over `mpsc`. No epoll/kqueue reactor
  (that would need raw syscalls); the thread-pool-plus-completion model is libuv's own fs
  strategy. Each turn drains microtasks, queued callbacks, due timers, and I/O completions,
  then blocks until the next event.
- **Timers** (`lumen-timers`) — `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`/
  `setImmediate`, plus `queueMicrotask`.
- **`console` and `process`** — streaming `console.*`; `process.argv`/`env`/`platform`/
  `cwd()`/`exit()`/`nextTick()`.
- **Filesystem** (`lumen-fs`) — synchronous ops (`readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`,
  `existsSync`, `mkdirSync`, `readdirSync`, …), file handles via a resource table
  (`openSync`/`readSync`/`writeSync`/`closeSync`), and async `fs.promises.readFile`/
  `writeFile` on the thread pool.
- **Web platform** (`lumen-web`) — a growing slice of the WinterTC Minimum Common API:
  `Event`/`EventTarget`/`CustomEvent`/`AbortController`/`AbortSignal`/`DOMException`,
  `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `atob`/`btoa`, `structuredClone`, `URL`/`URLSearchParams`,
  `performance.now()`, `crypto.getRandomValues`/`randomUUID`/`subtle.digest` (SHA-256), and
  `fetch`/`Headers`/`Request`/`Response`. See the checklist at the top of
  `crates/lumen-web/src/lib.rs` for what's implemented vs. deferred (streams, `Blob`/
  `FormData`, `URLPattern`, …).

  `fetch` speaks HTTP/1.1 over `std::net`. **`https:` is not supported**: TLS cannot be
  implemented on std alone and no third-party crate is permitted, so `https` URLs reject with
  a clear error; plain `http` works.

  `Lumen.serve((request) => Response)` is the matching HTTP/1.1 **server** — not a WinterTC API,
  but the cross-runtime `serve(handler)` convention (Deno/Bun/Workers), so a Hono app runs with
  `Lumen.serve(app.fetch)`. v1 is single-accept, `Connection: close`, buffered bodies, http only
  (see `crates/lumen-web/src/server.rs`). Cold-start and usage: `examples/hono-app`.

- **Modules — both CommonJS and ESM.** `lumen-cli` picks the module kind the way Node does:
  `.mjs` is ESM, `.cjs` is CommonJS, `.js` follows the nearest `package.json` `"type"`. ES
  modules run through the engine's real module graph (linking, top-level `await`); `import`
  specifiers resolve against disk and `node_modules`, `node:` builtins are importable
  (named imports included), and CommonJS packages interop by default export. CommonJS files
  run as the program entry with `require.main === module`.

- **`node:` compatibility** (`lumen-node`) — a CommonJS `require` with `node_modules`
  resolution and the module wrapper, `package.json` `main`/`exports`, the `node:path`/
  `node:os`/`node:fs` builtins, and `Buffer`, so packages written against the `node:` surface
  run. See the checklist at the top of `crates/lumen-node/src/lib.rs` for the deferred pieces
  (subpath-pattern exports, the full N-API surface).

  **Native addons** load too: `require('./addon.node')` dlopens the compiled library and runs its
  N-API registration, resolving the addon's `napi_*` symbols against the lumen executable — the
  same mechanism the `node` binary uses. The N-API surface is implemented from scratch (values,
  properties, functions, callbacks, errors, references, object wrap, classes, promises, buffers,
  typed arrays, async work); the loader reaches `dlopen`/`dlsym` through raw `extern "C"`
  declarations, so no third-party crate is added. See `examples/native-addon`.

  **`vite build` runs on lumen** (`examples/vite-app`): a full Vite production build, bundling
  through Rollup's native N-API addon, transforming with esbuild's service subprocess, over
  ESM↔CommonJS interop and the `node:` surface — building `dist/` and exiting cleanly.

- **REPL + CLI** (`lumen-repl`, `lumen-cli`) — an interactive shell with a persistent realm,
  parser-driven incomplete-input detection (multi-line continuation), top-level `await`, and
  loop-to-quiescence so timers and awaited promises settle before the next prompt. Line
  editing is line-buffered (raw-mode/history would need `termios`); use `rlwrap` for arrows
  and history.

### Workspace crates

```
lumen          engine (std-only, zero-dep; `embed` feature gates the runtime API)
lumen-host     substrate: OpState, ResourceTable, Extension, the thread-pool/callback primitives
lumen-timers   setTimeout/setInterval/queueMicrotask/setImmediate
lumen-fs       filesystem (sync + async)
lumen-web      WinterTC Minimum Common API (Event, URL, crypto, fetch, …)
lumen-node     node: compatibility (require, node:path/os/fs, Buffer)
lumen-runtime  the event loop; assembles the op crates; console + process
lumen-repl     interactive shell
lumen-cli      node/deno-style entrypoint

test262-runner   conformance harness (parallel workers over ./test262)
lumen-difftest   differential fuzzer across the three execution tiers
lumen-wasm       wasm build of the engine
```

The dependency graph is a strict DAG — `lumen ← lumen-host ← {op crates} ← lumen-runtime ←
lumen-repl ← lumen-cli` — so each op crate can be worked on in isolation.

Part 1 (the unicode module) is finished and installed in `/workspace/src/unicode/`. Every table I expose matches the original exactly in exhaustive tests. It builds without warnings when mounted as `mod unicode;`, and the 6 unit tests pass in debug and release. `/tmp/unicode_dev/DONE` has been touched.

**Files** (no other `/workspace` file touched; nothing committed):
- `/workspace/src/unicode/mod.rs` (38 KB): the API, the algorithms, and a doc header listing the quirks below.
- `/workspace/src/unicode/tables.rs` (146 KB, generated): compact varint strings, decoded lazily into cached sorted tables with binary search.
- The generator and probe scripts are in `/tmp/unicode_dev/gen/` and `/tmp/unicode_dev/`; the dev crate is `/tmp/unicode_dev/ucore`.

**API**: every required signature is present exactly as specified. `CaseMapping` is a `Copy` iterator over up to 3 code points. Extra public helpers:
- `simple_case_fold_class(c)` and `legacy_canonicalize_class(c)` return `Option<&'static [u32]>`, the full equivalence class, which the regexp side can use for /i closure.
- `string_property_ref(name)`: same as `string_property` but without copying.
- `has_property`, `script(c)`, `script_extensions(c)`, `canonical_combining_class`, `is_cased`, `is_case_ignorable`, `GeneralCategory::short_name`, `UNICODE_VERSION = (17,0,0)`.

**Where the data comes from and how it was checked**
- **Properties:** extracted from the original with `/\p{X}+/gu` over every code point. The 15.0 sources differ only at characters new in 16.0/17.0 or at known Unicode updates.
  - 1,724 accepted names/aliases compared range-for-range against the original: 0 mismatches.
  - 4,352 case and underscore variants of names checked for accept/reject: 0 mismatches.
- **Case mapping:** Rust std matches the original's `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase` for every code point (0 diffs).
- **Case folding:**
  - The /ui classes (1,454) and the non-unicode /i classes (1,144) come from the original and match exactly.
  - `simple_case_fold` uses the real CaseFolding targets, including the three foldings new in 16.0 (U+1FD3→U+0390, U+1FE3→U+03B0, U+FB05→U+FB06).
- **Normalization:** UCD 15.0 data plus the original's decompositions for the 20 new canonical and 36 new compatibility characters.
  - All four forms for every code point: 0 mismatches.
  - 150K random sequences (case mapping plus all four forms): 0 mismatches.
  - Reordering behaviour checked for every code point: identical.
- **Properties of strings:** the 15.0 lists all verified against the original. New sequences found by bulk-testing about 16M candidates, giving: Basic_Emoji 1219 singles / 219 strings, keycaps 12, modifier sequences 670, flags 259, tags 3, ZWJ sequences 1614, RGI_Emoji 1193 singles / 2760 strings.

**Quirks of the original, reproduced on purpose**
- Script values are matched loosely: case-insensitive and underscores ignored (`\p{sc=latin}`, `sc=OLD_ITALIC`, `sc=Latin__` are accepted). General_Category values and binary property names are strict. `WSpace`, `Hrkt` and `Katakana_Or_Hiragana` are rejected.
- `Basic_Emoji` includes the 26 regional indicators as single characters and `#️`, `*️`, `0️`–`9️` as strings. The modifier-sequence property includes 👪 plus a skin tone. `RGI_Emoji` excludes all of these, so it is stored as the union of the other six minus an exclusion list.
- Normalization combining classes are the 15.0 ones plus only 12 new non-zero values. Other marks added in 16.0/17.0 (e.g. U+1ACF, U+10EFA) act as class 0.
- Final sigma follows ICU: characters that are both cased and case-ignorable are skipped, and lone surrogates stop the scan.
- `normalize` passes lone surrogates through as starters that never compose.

**For the JS layer:**
- `normalize` with a bad form throws `RangeError: The normalization form should be one of NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD` (no trailing period); `normalize()` and `normalize(undefined)` mean NFC.
- The original's `readFileSync` and `writeFileSync` fail with "Invalid typed array length" above a few MB.
- Building an array of about 1.1M elements throws "array length exceeds engine limit".
